findings: The hero has mild focal competition: the oversized Didone 'André / Macedo' and the bright orange long-exposure arc both pull hard at the same altitude, so the eye ping-pongs before settling.
The orange light-trail photograph, while well-integrated, leans on a somewhat familiar long-exposure/light-painting aesthetic — the single most stock-ready element on the page.

The top running-metadata strip ('the sun 87° up · the tall arches are miami...') and the dense mono sub-blocks flirt with decorative noise; a visitor scanning fast reads them as texture, not information.
Section 2's self-screenshot is clever but at thumbnail size it reads as a muddy grey rectangle, weakening an otherwise sharp recursive idea.
what_works: Genuine high-contrast Didone display serif paired with a monospace utility voice — exactly the editorial-against-mono pairing a templated generator never reaches for; this is a real typographic point of view.

A sustained conceptual throughline (the photographic plate / long exposure) carried across the running shutter ticker, the radial star-trail generative diagram in §3, and the 'today's path over miami' plot in §4 — these are custom graphics, not garnish.

Asymmetric editorial composition anchored top-left with § section markers and numbered index tables (metallurgy, murmuration, meridians…) — confident left-rag layout rather than default-centered symmetry.
Warm amber accent held in strict reserve, surfacing only in the italic pivots ('stood still', 'comes back') and echoing the hero arc — one dominant harmony, disciplined.
Stranger test fully satisfied above the fold: name at display scale, a concrete one-liner on the two companies, and a live 'me@andremacedo.com' all legible without scrolling.
A.reasoning: This is unmistakably not a SaaS template: no centered hero, no gradient, no three-card row — instead a high-contrast Didone-and-mono editorial system with an asymmetric left-anchored grid, § section markers, and a conceptual long-exposure metaphor expressed through genuinely custom generative diagrams. The decisive moves (the Didone/mono pairing, the shutter-ticker header, the radial star-trail plot, the restrained amber accent) are things a default generator would not produce, and the first viewport cleanly delivers name, role, and email. It is held back from the top band only by hero focal competition and some mono clutter that reads as texture, but it clears the threshold and is not slop.

expressive pairing of refined serif display with crisp sans utility creates clear typographic voice
cohesive warm/dark-to-light color story with restrained orange accent feels intentional and tied to the photographic concept

B.reasoning: The desktop render is a thoughtful, metaphor-driven editorial experience built around the long-exposure/daguerreotype conceit. The hero image is genuinely strong and not template-grade. Typography and color show clear point of view. However, the long vertical composition dilutes focal hierarchy with several equally weighted visual moments, and the overall execution, while far above generic SaaS slop, still contains some rhythmic and scaling choices that feel tasteful but not rigorously masterful. No cardinal slop states are present. Overall a solid but not yet transcendent generation.
